Transformer T2 Camper Is Versatility Manifest – Lives up to Its Name and Serves Almost Any Purpose
14 photos
Photo: RD Trailers
Generally, travel trailers follow established design rules, but every once in a while, we come across a trinket that redefines how we approach glamping, and one RV that does just that is none other than Transformer T2 from RD trailers.
Campers, especially smaller ones, are usually governed by construction rules and when a camper goes against the grain, so to speak, and offers something different, we need to be all eyes and ears. Even more so considering the price of a standard T2.
According to the manufacturer’s website, the camper before us is priced starting at just $16,500 (€15,000), and since RD Trailers is one of those smaller teams, you can actually talk things over directly with them to craft the T2 of your dreams, which will clearly depend on the sort of lifestyle you’d like to live while out and about.
Photo: RD Trailers Now, those rules of construction and design which I mentioned mainly refer to how this thing is built and what tricks it has up its sleeve. At the heart of the T2 sits an aluminum frame with sidewalls that are welded directly to that frame. Sealing the sides in is a one-piece fiberglass floor and roof construction, so don’t worry about the elements seeping in.
Because of all this aluminum, the T2 is also rather light, rolling in with a dry weight of 1,500 lbs (680 kg) and able to handle a whopping 3,500 lbs (1,587 kg), granted by the presence of a torsion axle which can be upgraded.
The resulting abilities of the all-aluminum build, insulated sidewalls, and one-piece roof is that water and dust should have a hard time making their way inside your unit, but it also means one very strong construction, especially for the weight. There aren’t a whole lot of campers out there that can handle more than their own weight in cargo.
Photo: RD Trailers Speaking of cargo, it’s in this department that we also witness one of the tricks up the T2’s sleeve. If you’ve had a chance to peek at the images in the gallery, you’ll have spotted the fact that there’s a rear hatch in the T2’s construction, aside from two side doors.
Usually, these hatches hide kitchens, ones equipped with the necessary tools and systems we need to wash and clean dishes and veggies, toss on a couple of eggs and bacon, and even listen to music or fiddle with systems.
Well, you can forget all about this picturesque kitchen, and instead, be prepared to access the actual interior of this camper, directly from the rear. Just keep in mind that it’s NOT a downward opening gate, but a side-action one, so you won’t actually us it as a ramp to stuff items into your unit.
Photo: RD Trailers Instead, it will make for some of the best views from bed that a camper of this size can offer. Just point the rear toward east or west, depending on if you want to see the sunrise or sunset and just wait for the magic to happen.
Another benefit is that, yes, you can easily cram larger items into your camper including e-bikes, kayaks that’ll fit, and more. In essence, the T2 is a tailer that can be whatever it is you want but does start off without a mattress, so it’s more of a toy hauler, than anything else. Again, only in its more standard layout.
In truth, there isn’t anything in the spec sheet or options list about a bed, but that’s easily resolved with a modular mattress that you can find after your purchase, or tap into the E-tracks that run along the sides to whip up a unique bedding system. You don’t need much and can see the steps necessary here . Look into the skylight option if you do take this route.
Photo: RD Trailers Keep in mind that, due to the amount of cargo the T2 can handle, RD Trailers does invite owners to tap into the roof rack and free up the space inside with a roof-top tent. A great option to ensure you leave the interior untouched, but which does limit the camping seasons in which you’ll feel comfortable. Step-on fenders are in place to access roof-mounted gear and most tents do come with ladders.
While there is no galley in the T2 , all except a dry sink and swing-out system for a Blackstone grill, there is plenty of space for you to craft your own and bring along a fridge, cooktop, spice stash, and more.
Some features that are in place as standard include charge ports, CO2 detector, lights, an AGM battery, and plenty of space for the rest. Shore power is there too, and things like bike mounts can be added, not to mention solar power, annex bathrooms, and batwing awnings to offer shade all around the unit.
While we could talk about the T2 and just how far we can take one for a few hours, it’s best that I leave some details to your discovery and urge you to get in touch with RD Trailers if you’re looking for camper versatility manifest.
